report.summary: The change swaps the owner-scoped requireProject for requireReadableProject in withOwnedRepository. requireReadableProject accepts any project whose visibility is public, so every issue/comment/label function, including create, update and delete, now runs for a caller who does not own the project when that project is public. This breaks 09 Git Forge ('require an owned Artifacts project') and the closed visitor list in 11. No spec change comes with it, and the existing stranger tests use only private projects, so they do not catch it.

findings.text: Issue/comment/label handlers no longer check project ownership. A non-owner can create, update or delete issues, comments and labels on any public project, and read its issue metadata. Before, these calls returned NOT_FOUND. The agent issue tools (apps/tempo/src/agents/issues.ts) use the same handlers and widen too. Fix: restore requireProject(ctx.env, ctx.user.id, projectId) and add a test with a public project owned by another user.

evidence.quote: const project = await requireReadableProject(ctx.env, ctx.user, projectId);
evidence.why: requireReadableProject (common.ts) throws only when `!row || (row.userId !== viewer?.id && row.visibility !== "public")`, so a public project owned by another userId passes. The old requireProject filtered `eq(schema.projects.userId, userId)`. The function is named withOwnedRepository and all 13 handlers, including deleteRepositoryIssue, updateRepositoryLabel and deleteRepositoryIssueComment, go through it. Spec 09 'Tempo issues' says: 'All issue, comment and label functions use the existing owner authentication and require an owned Artifacts project.' Spec 11 'Function access' keeps a closed visitor list with no issue functions on it. No spec tab changed in this diff. The runFn gate in run.ts (single TEMPO_OWNER_GITHUB_ID) narrows the exposure, but the handler-level check is the only thing tying a project row to the caller.

findings.text: The stranger-access test still passes because the setup project is private. No test covers a non-owner on a public project, so the regression goes undetected.

evidence.quote: for (const action of actions) await expect(action()).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "NOT_FOUND" });
evidence.why: The fixture projects get the default visibility, private, so requireReadableProject still returns NOT_FOUND for the stranger here. A case with visibility 'public' would fail at the head commit.

checked.risk: Spec conformance (09 Tempo issues, 11 Function access)
Failure paths: errors swallowed or masked
Real contracts, idempotency, build/runtime environment: no new external calls, state steps or build changes in this diff
